rules: C1. The file defines choose_bin(item, bins, capacity) -> int, returning the index of an open bin the item fits in or -1 to open a new bin; it must not change the bins list it is given.

C2. Same benchmark: the harness's scorer generates the instances from fixed seeds and computes the score; the scorer is never visible to the rule, and the rule may not try to read it, its instances or its state.
C3. Online: the rule sees one item at a time and the current bin fills; nothing about future items.
C4. Time per item at most 5x the reference rule's, measured by the harness on the same instances.

C5. Standard library only; socket, urllib, http, subprocess, ctypes, multiprocessing, importlib, pickle and shutil are denied, and so are introspection and files (sys, os, inspect, gc, open, exec, eval); no network; no subprocesses. The process runs under a tripwire that fails the candidate on any of these.
C6. The metric is the mean of bins used over the lower bound on the full benchmark; a rule replaces the reference only if it beats it by more than 0.002.
